question_text: This is a still from the series, X. It depicts two techies lazing around at their workplace, which is shut down with no clients coming in. As such, they don't have much to do, so they're planning to steal their employer's asset and sell it for money. "We've got a buyer", Y says. "Some startup in Costa Rica". An incredulous Z asks: "How are we going to get that to Costa Rica?!" "Pieces man", Y responds, as he revs up his saw machine. Identify the show X (4 pts) and the actors playing Y and Z (6 pts). Accompanying image: a still showing two men in dark suits walking through a glass-walled corridor overlooking a lab-like space containing a large reptilian creature, with two other figures seated nearby.
answer_text: X: Westworld Season 3. Y and Z: David Benioff and D. B. Weiss, making a cameo appearance as the two techies. Connect to Singapore: Westworld Season 3 was shot extensively in Singapore.

question_text: Picture clue: a photo of a small black USB thumb drive with its cap removed, branded Trek ThumbDrive. The humble X has a highly contentious origin with 4 parties from different parts of the world laying claim to its invention. M-Systems, an Israeli firm, was granted a patent on November 14, 2000, and have been recognized by some as the inventors of X. Netac Technology filed a patent even earlier in 1999, which was granted by the Chinese government in 2002. Trek 2000 International is the first company known to have sold it commercially, and they branded it "X", which went on to become a genericized trademark; they have maintained they are the original inventors of X. And finally, Phison invented the first version that reduced the size and production cost of X, by using a single chip instead of multiple chips, in 2001. Identify X.
answer_text: Thumb drive / pen drive (USB flash drive). Connect to Singapore: Trek 2000, the company that sold and named the first thumb drive, is Singaporean.

question_text: Identify the footballer X from his extraordinary career (10 pts). He is the only player in the history of the sport to have scored in 6 continents in professional football. He has played top-flight football in 10 different countries, in no particular order: Brazil, Lithuania, Netherlands, Japan, Mexico, Azerbaijan, Italy, Bhutan, Russia, Australia. While still an active player, he managed the Cambodian men's national team for 5 years in a voluntary unpaid role; he held weekly conferences with the coaching staff and was on the touchline when Cambodia played during international breaks, and when he was unavailable, his assistant Felix Dalmas stepped in. He is also the co-founder of the investment firm X&KSK, which raised $98 million in 2025 to invest in AI start-ups. He is still an active player.
answer_text: Keisuke Honda. Connect to Singapore: Honda has just signed for the Singaporean club FC Jurong and is gunning to enter the Guinness book as the first player to score in 10 top division leagues.

question_text: Video still of an aerial shot of the Pentagon building. X: part of an iconic franchise, this teaser was released in 2015. Identify X (7 pts). Y: which real-life figure, who was in the news in the mid-2010s, is the guy who's talking in the teaser inspired from? (3 pts)
answer_text: X: Call of Duty: Black Ops 3 (teaser trailer). Y: Edward Snowden. Connect to Singapore: Call of Duty: Black Ops 3 is set primarily in Singapore (and Cairo). Also, Edward Snowden exposed Singapore's role in providing secret access to Malaysia's communications data to the US.

question_text: X's linguistic experimentation of mixing other languages along with English prose was present from his very first novel, Y, which featured Malay words and phrases without immediate translation, forcing readers to absorb the terms through context. This style was taken to a whole new level in his most acclaimed novel Z, where teenage delinquents narrate their violent exploits in a fictional 'argot' called Nadsat which combines Slavic loanwords, Cockney rhyming slang, and baby talk. The argot was maintained in the equally popular movie adaptation released nine years later. Identify X (3 pts), his debut novel Y (5 pts), and the more acclaimed novel Z (2 pts).
answer_text: X: Anthony Burgess. Y: Time for a Tiger, his debut novel and first of the Malayan trilogy. Z: A Clockwork Orange. Connect to Singapore: Time for a Tiger borrows its title from the iconic tagline of the Singaporean beer brand, Tiger Beer.

question_text: Identify X (6 pts) and Y (4 pts). The idea of putting a X in a blank blank came after Y saw an industrial sawmill at the Bath branch of timber importers, Hill Leigh Ltd. Although this company was liquidated in August 2012, it was bought by Travis Perkins Builders Merchants who still maintain a working sawmill on the site to this day. Y described this moment of inspiration in an interview with the Guardian in 2016: "One day I was at a local sawmill and noticed how the sawdust was being removed from the air by large industrial X. My engineering instinct kicked in. Could that work on a smaller scale?"
answer_text: X: Cyclone (cyclonic separation technology). Y: James Dyson, inventor of the Dyson bagless cyclone vacuum cleaner. Connect to Singapore: Dyson is headquartered in Singapore. James Dyson also owned the costliest house in Singapore for a while, before returning to the UK.

question_text: Photo of Michael Phelps and two other swimmers on an Olympic podium, all raising joined hands. This iconic photo was taken right after Michael Phelps' last ever individual Olympic event, the 100m butterfly, at the 2016 Olympics. However, this race was historic for one more reason: it saw something that had never happened before in Olympic swimming, or since. Give funda (10 pts). The other swimmers in the photo are Chad le Clos of South Africa and Laszlo Cseh of Hungary.
answer_text: A historic three-way tie for the silver medal, with Michael Phelps, Chad le Clos, and Laszlo Cseh all finishing at 51.14 seconds, behind gold medallist Joseph Schooling. Connect to Singapore: Joseph Schooling beat all three of them to gold, becoming the first, and so far only, Singaporean Olympic gold medallist.

question_text: Still from a 1970s martial arts/spy film showing a group of women in white robes running through a forest, captioned 'Fights like a panther'. They Call Her 'X' Wong is a 1978 spy film made by the Filipino director Bobby Suarez. It features the adventures of Interpol agent X Wong and rode on the back of the popularity of the Bond films of the time, Hong Kong martial arts films, and the blaxploitation films of the era. The titular character X shares her name with a historical figure who has parallels with her story: both strong-willed women who conquer powerful male foes from around the world. The film's action scenes and costume design served as a "gigantic inspiration" for the iconic movie Y, according to its director. Identify X (6 pts) and Y (4 pts).
answer_text: X: Cleopatra Wong (the film is They Call Her Cleopatra Wong). Y: Kill Bill. Connect to Singapore: both Cleopatra Wong and the actress who played her, Marrie Lee, are Singaporean.

question_text: A Google Trends graph titled 'Google Trends Interest Over Time for ___' (song title covered by a redaction bar) showing interest spikes annotated with dates: first singing it in July 2019 at a GP, singing during a GP in August 2019, finishing P3 from P20 on the grid and singing in victory at the November 2019 Brazil GP, singing during the April 2021 Italian GP, bringing the song back after a win in September 2023, and another spike around March 2024. The song X, which released in 1984, saw a surge in popularity when Y sang it in public in July 2019 in London, revealing that it had been playing repeatedly on the radio. He sang it again in the next few months in cities as diverse as Budapest and Sao Paulo. The song went viral again in 2023, almost 40 years after its release, when Y sang it again after a hiatus; this was also the period when TikTok edits featuring Y and the song went viral. Identify the song X (5 pts) and the singer Y (5 pts).
answer_text: X: Smooth Operator by Sade. Y: Carlos Sainz, the Formula 1 driver known for singing the song over team radio after race wins. Connect to Singapore: Smooth Operator became viral again after a lull when Sainz won the 2023 Singapore GP and sang it over the team radio; it was the only race that Red Bull failed to win that entire season.

question_text: Image of a set of unreleased postage stamps depicting, in order: a soldier aiming a rifle; farmers ploughing with cattle; a woman at a spinning wheel; a nurse tending to a patient; a map of India wrapped in chains; and a design (partly hidden behind a teal box) of a tiger leaping across a flag reading 'AZAD' over 'HIND', held aloft by three soldiers. What are these the unreleased stamps of? (10 pts).
answer_text: The unreleased postage stamps of Azad Hind, the Provisional Government of Free India led by Subhas Chandra Bose. Connect to Singapore: Azad Hind was established in Japanese-controlled Singapore in 1943.

question_text: Few records in ODI cricket lasted as long as Shahid Afridi's fastest century (37 balls) vs. Sri Lanka in the 1996 KCA Centenary Tournament in Nairobi; the record stood for a staggering 17 years. The previous record for the fastest ODI century lasted nowhere as long though. It belonged to X, who blitzed a 48-ball ton only six months earlier. X broke the record of Y, an Indian batsman, who previously held the record for scoring a 62-ball century vs. New Zealand. Identify X and Y (5 pts each). Coincidentally, Y was X's first ever wicket in ODI cricket.
answer_text: X: Sanath Jayasuriya. Y: Mohammad Azharuddin. Connect to Singapore: Jayasuriya scored his record-breaking century at the Padang Ground, Singapore, also where Sachin Tendulkar famously scored a century vs. Pakistan in the 1996 Singer Cup, and where Ricardo Powell scored a blistering century in the 1999 Singapore Challenge final vs India.

question_text: The American TV producer Glen A. Larson had been pitching a series of television films titled Adam's Ark that blended science fiction with Mormon theology ever since the late 1960s. He didn't find any takers for his idea till a decade later, when, stunned by the success of "A B", Universal Studios gave him an unprecedented $1m per episode to produce it. One of the conditions given to him was to change the show's title: the mandate was to include the word "A" in the title to capitalize on the success of "A B". The show X was thus born, though it was cancelled after a single season. The primary antagonists of X are the Y, originally conceived as biological reptilian aliens, with the goal of wiping off the human race. However, ABC's Broadcast Standards did not allow humans killing Y, as it would have constituted "body count" and graphic slaughter during family hour on TV. They were thus made robots instead, which would constitute destroying property as opposed to killing. Identify the show X (6 pts) and the antagonists Y (4 pts).
answer_text: X: Battlestar Galactica. Y: the Cylons. ("A B" refers to Star Wars.) Connect to Singapore: the Battlestar Galactica: Human vs Cylon ride at Universal Studios Singapore is the only ride in the world based on the show, and is also the world's duelling roller coaster.

question_text: What's the connect? (10 pts). Soil from: Jerusalem; Mecca; Lake Manasarovar, Tibet; Golden Temple site, Amritsar; Vaishnodevi, J&K; Dargah Shareef, Ajmer; Medak Cathedral, Telangana; Parliament House Complex, New Delhi; Porbandar, Gujarat; Nadiad, Gujarat; Cuttack, Odisha; Mhow, Madhya Pradesh; Allahabad, UP; Rameswaram, TN.
answer_text: The inauguration of Amaravati, capital of Andhra Pradesh (soil and water from these religiously and historically significant sites across India were used in the foundation ceremony). Connect to Singapore: the governments of Andhra Pradesh and Singapore signed an MOU to help design and plan Amaravati; the MOU was later cancelled, with Singapore now operating as a technical advisor.

question_text: The 'X curse' is a popular urban legend stating that any company, product, or brand the star endorses is destined to face sudden bankruptcy, severe scandals, or commercial failure. Examples: Mitsubishi recalled more than 23,000 Pajero SUVs over airbag inflator safety concerns; Bawang Shampoo suffered a huge drop in sales after media reports claimed its products could cause cancer; the food brand Synyear, which produces sweet dumplings, was ordered to pull one of its products off shelves after traces of Staphylococcus aureus were found; the gym chain California Fitness went out of business and was sued for unpaid rents by its landlords; more examples include Volkswagen Caddy, Fen Huang Cola, Ai-duo VCD Electronics, etc. Naturally, there were concerns when he was announced as the brand ambassador of Y in 2021. However, the first ad released in September 2021 was a massive success and the partnership was instantly renewed. The brand had done a similar viral campaign two years earlier with another global star, prompting the violent "THAT'S NOT MY GOAT! THAT'S NOT MY GOAT!" reaction from IShowSpeed. Identify X the star (5 pts) and Y the brand (5 pts).
answer_text: X: Jackie Chan, subject of the 'Jackie Chan curse'. Y: Shopee. Connect to Singapore: Shopee, one of the world's largest e-commerce platforms, is Singaporean.

question_text: Aerial photo of a compact cricket stadium on a waterfront beside a beach, with hills in the background. X, one of the most picturesque stadiums in the world, is named after the beach next to it. While the stadium overall is quite compact, its straight boundary distance is among the longest in the world at 82m; in fact, its playing surface is THE longest of any active international cricket stadium at 175m. Y, however, made a mockery of the long boundary by hitting a scarcely believable 129m six here in 2025, beating the record for the longest six in a T20I. Identify the stadium X and the player Y (5 pts each).
answer_text: X: Bellerive Oval (Blundstone Arena), Hobart. Y: Tim David. Connect to Singapore: Tim David played international cricket for Singapore from 2019-20 and was born in Singapore.

question_text: The 2024 Met Gala took place in May 2024 at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City. The co-chairs of the event, who helped Anna Wintour curate the guest list, set the theme, helped with hosting duties and manage fundraising, were: Zendaya; Bad Bunny, the Puerto Rican musician and Grammy winner; Chris Hemsworth; Jennifer Lopez; Jonathan Anderson, Creative Director of the luxury fashion house Loewe; and X, CEO of (company name blanked out). Only months ago, X had gone globally viral during a tense exchange that nearly became a global geopolitical incident. Identify X (4 pts) and the viral incident from January 2024 (6 pts).
answer_text: X: Shou Zi Chew, CEO of TikTok. The viral incident: during a US Senate hearing, when pressed by a senator about ties to the Chinese government, he replied "Senator, I'm Singaporean." Connect to Singapore: Shou Zi Chew is, of course, Singaporean, though Senator Tom Cotton (the senator in the exchange) doesn't agree.
